# Modifying

Rearranging a slice in place, removing elements, and moving elements between slices.

<h2 id="swap"><code>Swap&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Swap<T>(left: *var T, right: *var T)
```

Exchanges the values at two locations.
Both are borrowed mutably and both are written. Passing the same location twice is legal and leaves it alone.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.
Both pointers must be non-null and writable.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Modify.rux#L20)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type     | Description             |
| ------- | -------- | ----------------------- |
| `left`  | `*var T` | one of the two elements |
| `right` | `*var T` | the other               |

<h2 id="reverse"><code>Reverse&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Reverse<T>(items: var T[..])
```

Reverses the order of `items` in place.
`items` is borrowed mutably and rewritten. An empty slice and a single element are already reversed, so neither
is a special case.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length, making half as many exchanges, and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Modify.rux#L33)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description             |
| ------- | ----------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `var T[..]` | the sequence to work on |

<h2 id="rotate"><code>Rotate&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Rotate<T>(items: var T[..], middle: uint) -> bool
```

Rotates `items` left so that the element at `middle` becomes the first.
`items` is borrowed mutably and rewritten. A `middle` of zero or of the whole length leaves the order alone;
anything past the length is refused, since there is no such element to bring to the front.
Done as three reversals — the front, the back, then the whole — which needs no scratch storage and touches
every element at most twice.
Reports false only for a `middle` past the length.
Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Modify.rux#L56)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type        | Description                                  |
| -------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `items`  | `var T[..]` | the sequence to work on                      |
| `middle` | `uint`      | the index that becomes the new first element |

**Returns**: whether `middle` was a usable index

<h2 id="fill"><code>Fill&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Fill<T>(items: var T[..], value: T)
```

Writes `value` into every position of `items`.
`items` is borrowed mutably and rewritten; `value` is read by value and copied into each position. An empty slice
writes nothing.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Modify.rux#L73)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description                         |
| ------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `items` | `var T[..]` | the sequence to work on             |
| `value` | `T`         | the value to write to every element |

<h2 id="copy-to"><code>CopyTo&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CopyTo<T>(
    destination: var T[..],
    source: T[..]
) -> bool
```

Copies `source` into `destination`, front to back.
`destination` is borrowed mutably and written; `source` is borrowed and read. Reports false when the two lengths
differ, having written nothing: a partial copy is worse than a refused one, since the caller cannot tell how far
it got.
The two must not overlap, unless `destination` begins at or before `source`. Use [`MoveTo`](/docs/api/algorithms/modifying#move-to) where they might.
Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.
Overlapping the wrong way silently copies elements that were already overwritten.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Modify.rux#L93)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type        | Description                  |
| ------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `destination` | `var T[..]` | where the results go         |
| `source`      | `T[..]`     | where the elements come from |

**Returns**: whether `destination` was long enough

<h2 id="move-to"><code>MoveTo&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func MoveTo<T>(
    destination: var T[..],
    source: T[..]
) -> bool
```

Copies `source` into `destination`, correctly however the two overlap.
`destination` is borrowed mutably and written; `source` is borrowed and read. Reports false when the two lengths
differ, having written nothing.
Copies back to front when `destination` starts after `source`, and front to back otherwise, which is what makes
shifting a run of elements along its own storage safe in either direction.
Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Modify.rux#L114)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name          | Type        | Description                  |
| ------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `destination` | `var T[..]` | where the results go         |
| `source`      | `T[..]`     | where the elements come from |

**Returns**: whether `destination` was long enough

<h2 id="unique"><code>Unique&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Unique<T>(items: var T[..]) -> uint
```

Collapses each run of adjacent equal elements in `items` to one, and reports how many are left.
`items` is borrowed mutably and rewritten. Only _adjacent_ duplicates go: on a sorted slice that removes every
duplicate, and on an unsorted one it removes only the runs, which is the useful behaviour rather than a
compromise — it makes this the second half of sort-then-unique without paying for a second sort.
Relative order among the survivors is preserved, nothing is resized, and what lies past the reported length is
unspecified.
Requires `==` on the element type.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Modify.rux#L137)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description             |
| ------- | ----------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `var T[..]` | the sequence to work on |

**Returns**: how many elements are left after collapsing each run of equal neighbours to one

<h2 id="remove-value"><code>RemoveValue&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func RemoveValue<T>(items: var T[..], value: T) -> uint
```

Removes every element of `items` equal to `value`, and reports how many are left.
`items` is borrowed mutably and rewritten; `value` is read by value. Survivors are compacted toward the front in
their original order, nothing is resized, and what lies past the reported length is unspecified.
Requires `==` on the element type.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Modify.rux#L161)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description                             |
| ------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `items` | `var T[..]` | the sequence to work on                 |
| `value` | `T`         | the value to remove every occurrence of |

**Returns**: how many elements are left

<h2 id="remove-where"><code>RemoveWhere&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func RemoveWhere<T>(
    items: var T[..],
    predicate: func(T) -> bool
) -> uint
```

Removes every element of `items` that `predicate` accepts, and reports how many are left.
`items` is borrowed mutably and rewritten; `predicate` is called once per element. Survivors are compacted toward
the front in their original order, nothing is resized, and what lies past the reported length is unspecified.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `predicate` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Modify.rux#L183)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type              | Description                     |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `items`     | `var T[..]`       | the sequence to work on         |
| `predicate` | `func(T) -> bool` | the test each element is put to |

**Returns**: how many elements are left

<h2 id="partition"><code>Partition&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Partition<T>(
    items: var T[..],
    predicate: func(T) -> bool
) -> uint
```

Moves every element `predicate` accepts to the front of `items`, and reports how many there were.
`items` is borrowed mutably and rewritten; `predicate` is called once per element. Everything before the reported
index satisfies the predicate and everything from it on does not.
Order within each group is _not_ preserved: this exchanges elements from both ends inward, which is what keeps it
to one pass and no scratch storage. A caller that needs the original order within each group needs a stable
partition, which needs somewhere to put things.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `predicate` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Modify.rux#L208)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type              | Description                     |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `items`     | `var T[..]`       | the sequence to work on         |
| `predicate` | `func(T) -> bool` | the test each element is put to |

**Returns**: the index of the first element that fails `predicate`

<h2 id="partition-point"><code>PartitionPoint&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func PartitionPoint<T>(
    items: T[..],
    predicate: func(T) -> bool
) -> uint
```

Where the accepted elements of an already-partitioned `items` end.
`items` is borrowed and read; `predicate` is called about as many times as the logarithm of the length. Requires
that every element the predicate accepts comes before every element it rejects — which is what [`Partition`](/docs/api/algorithms/modifying#partition)
leaves behind, and what a sorted slice is with respect to any threshold predicate.
A slice that is not partitioned this way does not fail; it answers, and the answer is meaningless.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the logarithm of the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever
`predicate` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Modify.rux#L235)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type              | Description                     |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `items`     | `T[..]`           | the sequence to work on         |
| `predicate` | `func(T) -> bool` | the test each element is put to |

**Returns**: the index of the first element that fails `predicate`, assuming the sequence is partitioned
